advice: Propose: Base on `existing-sme`, SHA-256 `3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258`. Add an n=512-only path that packs both operands into 32-wide K-major panels inside `gemm`, then computes each 32×32 output tile from those panels. Keep the existing transpose-and-compute path as the general fallback. Each pair of panels is 131072 bytes, equal to the reported P-core L1D capacity; whether this layout improves locality after packing costs is unknown. This is distinct from the rejected paired-load-only change. Check generated assembly and spills, correctness at tolerance 0.002 including tails, guards, and n<=0, and fresh repeated paired AC measurements with packing inside the timed call. The measured history shows large baseline variation (1389.66, 933.69, 878.32 GFLOP/s); use unchanged controls and do not claim a gain from the hypothesis or instruction counts.
risks: Packing may cost more than any locality benefit, and the combined panels leave no L1D capacity margin. The proposal is unverified; no causal speedup claim is supported. Preserve FP32 arithmetic, ABI, thread count, flags, and all benchmark gates.
